entry.title: Incident: Slowness searching with Slack AI
entry.summary: Issue Summary:From 6:30 PM PST on January 28, 2025 to around 11:00 AM PST on January 30, 2025, some Slack AI customers may have experienced issues with Slack AI searches.A configuration issue with some of our Slack AI infrastructure resulted in an unexpected backlog of Slack AI tasks. This backlog meant that Slack AI responses were not served to users in a timely manner. Additionally, certain Slack AI queries had very long timeout windows, remaining in the queue indefinitely and contributing to the backlog. We scaled up our Slack AI infrastructure to increase our capacity to work through the backlog and manually ended any stuck queries. We also deployed a code change to set more reasonable timeout windows for the long-running queries, resolving the issue for all impacted users.

entry.title: RESOLVED: **Summary:** Google Drive, Gmail Web, - Unable to see PDF annotations. **Description:** We are experiencing an issue with Google Drive, Gmail beginning at Wednesday, 2025-01-29 13:24 US/Pacific. Our engineering team continues to investigate the issue. We will provide an update by Wednesday, 2025-01-29 15:00 US/Pacific with current details. We apologize to all who are affected by the disruption. **Diagnosis:** Customers using Drive Web, Gmail Web, opening PDFs would not see PDF Annotations (shapes, user added text, freehand drawing, etc). All PDF data is still available. **Workaround:** Open the PDF in a different tool.
entry.summary:
Incident began at 2025-01-27 17:00 and ended at 2025-01-30 05:00 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Mini Incident Report

We apologize for the inconvenience this service disruption/outage may have caused. We would like to provide some information about this incident below. Please note, this information is based on our best knowledge at the time of posting and is subject to change as our investigation continues. If you have experienced impact outside of what is listed below, please reach out to Google Workspace Support using the help article https://support.google.com/a/answer/1047213.

(All Times US/Pacific)

Incident Start: 27 Jan 2025 09:00

Incident End: 29 Jan 2025 21:00

Duration: 2 days, 12 hours

Affected Services and Features:

Google Drive, Gmail

Regions/Zones: Global

Description:

Users experienced an issue where PDF annotations were not displayed when using Google Drive Web and Gmail Web for a period of 2 days, 12 hours. All PDF data was still available if downloaded.

A preliminary analysis indicates the incident was caused by a code change that incorrectly determined which portions of a PDF to display.

Google engineers mitigated the issue by rolling back the affected client builds and deployed a preventative server fix to ensure this incident does not occur again.

Customer Impact:

Affected users were unable to see PDF annotations, such as filled form fields, shapes, freehand drawing, in the previewer.

Affected products: Gmail, Google Drive

entry.title: Incident: Some iOS Users Unable to See Message Field and Send Messages
entry.summary: From January 25, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, to January 27, 2025 at 8:00 AM PST, users on iOS 16 were unable to send messages in the Slack for iOS app after updating to version 25.01.40.We introduced some updates to the message composer in app version 25.01.40. However, these changes inadvertently caused a conflict with earlier workarounds intended to mitigate known issues with the iOS 16 keyboard. This caused the message composer to disappear when users tried to type messages.We implemented a fix to remove this conflict in app version 25.01.41, which resolved the issue for all impacted users.

entry.title: Incident: Some users may be experiencing issues with their sidebar not being badged for new DMs and channel notifications.
entry.summary: Beginning around November 22, 2024 until January 16, 2025, some users on the desktop versions of Slack experienced unexpected behavior with sidebar bolding & badging for direct messages (DMs), group DMs, and channels. This caused users to miss unread messages within these conversations.We initially were tracking reports from affected users, but on January 6, 2025, we noticed an unexpected increase of reports causing us to initiate our incident response processes.As an initial fix, we rolled out a change to the backend logic to correct the timestamp and store correct values so the client triggered the appropriate badging & bolding notifications. While this fix resolved the initial badging & bolding behavior, it unexpectedly caused an issue with badging counts, resulting in displaying an incorrect number of unread messages as well as not marking a channels read state correctly. We promptly reversed this change to avoid further impact.We continued our investigation efforts and discovered an additional cause within the backend logic checks related to how a message is routed to the client. This check ensures the client is fetching the proper information that triggers the notification badging & bolding. We adjusted the problematic logic within this check to ensure the proper data is fetched when triggering a notification, resolving the issue for affected users.Throughout this incident, we adjusted our strategy on how to best handle incoming reports from affected users, which impacted updates on our status site. As more users reported experiencing this issue, we then resumed our status site updates.We apologize for any confusion and disruptions to your work day and appreciate your patience as we worked to resolve this issue for all affected users.

entry.summary: Jan 21, 22:21 UTC Resolved - Prior to Tuesday, January 21, 2025 at 19:20 UTC, customers that used an AWS CLI or AWS SDK version released on or after January 15, 2025 may have experienced issues with uploading files to a Spaces bucket. This impacted PutObject and UploadPart requests initiated by recent versions of the AWS CLI and AWS SDKs. Our Engineering team has confirmed resolution of this issue for almost all Spaces buckets (including all new Spaces buckets), which are now compatible with the latest versions of the AWS CLI and AWS SDKs (and tools and applications that depend on these versions). entry.title: Incident: Scheduled workflows not triggering
entry.summary: On January 6, from 3:23 AM PST to 4:50 PM PST scheduled workflows were not triggering correctly for some users.We identified that a recent update to our internal infrastructure had added unexpected load to the backend database that processes workflow triggers, which was causing scheduled workflows to fail.To mitigate further issues, we cleared these failed triggers from our systems. However, this inadvertently caused some workflows to re-trigger outside their scheduled time on customer’s workspaces.Once these failed triggers had been fully removed, we confirmed that scheduled workflows were working as expected again.

entry.title: Incident: Some users cannot switch between workspaces
entry.summary: On January 6, 2025 from 12:14 AM PST to 11:09 AM PST, some customers were unable to switch between workspaces on desktop.We identified that an error had been introduced via a routine code change that prevented an upgrade prompt from closing as expected. As the upgrade modal retained focus while open, this prevented users with a workspace on the free plan from switching between workspaces.We reverted the code change and the issue was resolved for all impacted users.
